questions.question: Design Splitwise — an expense-sharing app (LLD).
questions.title: Design Splitwise — Low-Level Design
questions.direct_answer: Model Splitwise around three entities: **`User`**, **`Group`**, and **`Expense`**. An expense has a payer, a total amount, and a **`SplitStrategy`** (`EQUAL`, `EXACT`, `PERCENT`, `SHARES`) that breaks the total into per-user shares. The system maintains a **`BalanceSheet`** — a directed map of `userA → userB → amount` — updated incrementally as expenses are added. **Settling up** uses a **simplification algorithm** (greedy max-creditor / max-debtor matching) to minimize the number of transfers. Use **interfaces for SplitStrategy and SettlementStrategy** for extensibility. Concurrency: per-group lock when mutating balances. For multi-currency, store amounts in their original currency and convert at view time. The whole design fits cleanly into a domain-driven, hexagonal Java app.

interviewer_intent.testing: Decomposition into User/Group/Expense, multiple split strategies via the Strategy pattern, balance sheet maintenance, and the simplification algorithm to minimize transfers.
interviewer_intent.common_mistake: One God class doing splits + balances + settlement; rounding errors in equal splits; quadratic 'who owes whom' computation done from scratch on every read.
interviewer_intent.to_stand_out: Discuss the simplification algorithm explicitly (greedy two-pointer on creditors/debtors), rounding-remainder distribution rules, multi-currency handling, and incremental balance updates.

sections.title: Problem Framing
sections.content:
Splitwise tracks who paid for what among a group of friends and who owes whom. The interesting design pressure is:

- **Multiple split modes** — equal, exact amounts, percent, shares — pluggable.
- **Maintaining the balance sheet incrementally** — don't recompute from scratch every time.
- **Settling up** — if four people have a tangled web of debts, can we minimize the number of payments? Yes, via simplification.
- **Edge cases** — rounding when splitting $10 among 3 people; multi-currency; payer who is also a participant.

At the LLD level, treat this as a single-instance OO design unless the interviewer pushes you to talk about scale. The strategy choices and the simplification algorithm are the grade.

sections.title: Clarifying Questions
sections.content:
- **Groups required**, or can two friends split outside any group?
- **Split modes:** equal, exact amount per person, percentage, shares (e.g., A:2, B:1)?
- **Currency:** single or multi-currency?
- **Settlement:** record cash repayments? Compute simplification (minimum number of transfers)?
- **Edit / delete expenses:** in scope? (Adds reconciliation complexity.)
- **Persistence:** in-memory for the interview is fine?
- **Concurrency:** multiple users in a group adding expenses simultaneously?

sections.title: Assumptions
sections.content:
- Expenses live in a `Group`. Two-friend splits modeled as a special group.
- Four split modes: `EQUAL`, `EXACT`, `PERCENT`, `SHARES`.
- Single currency for the core design; multi-currency called out as an extension.
- Settling up records cash repayments and supports simplification on demand.
- Edits / deletes called out as an extension (require reversal of the original split).
- In-memory state with a `GroupRepository` interface for persistence.
- Concurrent expense additions in the same group; per-group lock on balance updates.

sections.title: Core Entities and Responsibilities
sections.content:
- **`User`** — immutable id + name + email.
- **`Group`** — list of members, list of expenses, and a `BalanceSheet`.
- **`Expense`** — immutable record (id, payer, total amount, currency, description, splits per participant, timestamp).
- **`Split`** — (user, amount). Sum of splits == expense total.
- **`SplitStrategy`** (interface) — `computeSplits(total, participants, params) → List<Split>`. One implementation per mode.
- **`BalanceSheet`** — `Map<UserId, Map<UserId, Money>>` representing 'A owes B'. Incremental updates on expense add; supports `netBalance(userA, userB)`.
- **`SettlementStrategy`** (interface) — `simplify(BalanceSheet) → List<Transfer>`. Default implementation = greedy creditor/debtor matching.
- **`Transfer`** — (from, to, amount).
- **`SplitwiseService`** — use-case facade: `addExpense`, `recordSettlement`, `getBalances`, `getSimplifiedTransfers`.

sections.title: Class Diagram
sections.content:
```mermaid
classDiagram
    class User {
        +UserId id
        +String name
        +String email
    }
    class Group {
        +GroupId id
        +String name
        +Set~UserId~ members
        +List~Expense~ expenses
        +BalanceSheet balances
        +addExpense(Expense)
    }
    class Expense {
        +ExpenseId id
        +UserId paidBy
        +Money total
        +List~Split~ splits
        +String description
        +Instant createdAt
    }
    class Split {
        +UserId user
        +Money amount
    }
    class SplitStrategy {
        <<interface>>
        +computeSplits(total, participants, params) List~Split~
    }
    class BalanceSheet {
        +applyExpense(Expense)
        +applyTransfer(Transfer)
        +netBalance(a, b) Money
        +allBalances() Map
    }
    class SettlementStrategy {
        <<interface>>
        +simplify(BalanceSheet) List~Transfer~
    }
    class SplitwiseService {
        +addExpense(...)
        +recordSettlement(...)
        +getBalances(group)
        +getSimplifiedTransfers(group)
    }

    Group --> Expense
    Group --> BalanceSheet
    Expense --> Split
    SplitwiseService --> Group
    SplitwiseService --> SplitStrategy
    SplitwiseService --> SettlementStrategy
    EqualSplit ..|> SplitStrategy
    ExactSplit ..|> SplitStrategy
    PercentSplit ..|> SplitStrategy
    SharesSplit ..|> SplitStrategy
    GreedySettlement ..|> SettlementStrategy
```

sections.title: Split Strategies
Balance Sheet — Incremental Updates
Settle Up — Greedy Simplification
End-to-End Flow — Add Expense + View Settlement
sections.content:
```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant A as Alice (payer)
    participant Svc as SplitwiseService
    participant Strat as EqualSplit
    participant G as Group
    participant Bal as BalanceSheet

    A->>Svc: addExpense(group, paidBy=Alice, total=$30, EQUAL, [Alice,Bob,Carol])
    Svc->>Strat: computeSplits($30, [Alice,Bob,Carol])
    Strat-->>Svc: [Alice $10, Bob $10, Carol $10]
    Svc->>G: addExpense(expense)
    G->>Bal: applyExpense(expense)
    Bal->>Bal: Bob → Alice +$10; Carol → Alice +$10

    Note over A: Later, time to settle
    A->>Svc: getSimplifiedTransfers(group)
    Svc->>Bal: net per user
    Svc-->>A: [Bob → Alice $10, Carol → Alice $10]

    Note over A: Bob actually pays Alice
    A->>Svc: recordSettlement(Transfer(Bob → Alice $10))
    Svc->>Bal: applyTransfer
    Bal->>Bal: Bob's debt to Alice cleared
```

sections.title: Concurrency
Failure Modes and Edge Cases
sections.content:
- **Rounding remainder:** equal split of $10 among 3 → [$3.34, $3.33, $3.33]. Document the rule (extra cent goes to the first N users, deterministic).
- **Payer in participants:** payer's own split doesn't generate a debt to themselves — skip in `applyExpense`.
- **Edit / delete expense:** apply the reverse expense (subtract from balances), then apply the new one. Keep an audit log; never lose history.
- **Multi-currency:** store original-currency amounts in the expense; balance sheet stays in original currency. Conversion is a *view* concern, not a storage concern. Settlement strategy needs to handle multi-currency or normalize first.
- **Floating point:** never. Use `BigDecimal` (cents) or a custom `Money` value object.
- **Cycle of debts:** simplification handles this naturally — nets to zero → no transfer.
- **Self-transfer:** `Transfer(A → A)` is invalid; reject at construction.
- **User leaving group with non-zero balance:** require settlement first; record their final transfer log.

sections.title: Extensibility
sections.content:
- **New split mode** (e.g., `ITEMIZED` for a restaurant bill where each line maps to one or more eaters): new `SplitStrategy` implementation. No other code changes.
- **New settlement strategy** (e.g., minimize number of transfers but constrained to existing creditor/debtor edges only): new `SettlementStrategy`.
- **Multi-currency:** introduce a `CurrencyConverter` port; balance sheet remains per-currency or converts at view time.
- **Reminders / notifications:** publish `BalanceUpdatedEvent` when a transfer makes someone's balance large or stale.
- **Receipt OCR or auto-import:** an `ExpenseSource` adapter parses receipts and produces `Expense` objects.
- **Analytics:** expense history per group / per user becomes a CQRS read model; main aggregate stays clean.

sections.title: Trade-offs and Alternatives
sections.content:
- **Incremental matrix vs recompute on read:** incremental is O(1) reads but requires careful update logic. Recompute on read is simple but O(N²) per query. For active groups, incremental wins.
- **Greedy simplification vs optimal (NP):** greedy is near-optimal in practice; optimal is exponential and not worth it.
- **In-memory vs persistent:** in-memory fine for interview; production wraps `Group` in a JPA aggregate with a `BalanceSheetEmbeddable` and `@Version`.
- **Strategy interface vs enum + switch:** Strategy scales as modes grow and lets each mode's params live with its implementation; enum + switch fits two modes, then bloats.
- **Per-group lock vs lock-free:** lock is correct and simple; lock-free is overkill for a domain where contention is rare per-group.
- **Single-currency vs multi-currency:** single-currency is the right starting point. Multi-currency adds conversion semantics that should be a deliberate design decision, not an afterthought.

sections.title: Key Points
sections.content:
- **Three core entities:** `User`, `Group`, `Expense`.
- **`SplitStrategy` interface** with `EqualSplit`, `ExactSplit`, `PercentSplit`, `SharesSplit`.
- **`BalanceSheet` updated incrementally** on each expense / transfer; normalized so only one direction per pair is non-zero.
- **`SettlementStrategy` (greedy max-creditor / max-debtor)** minimizes transfers in O(N log N).
- **Rounding rule documented** for `EqualSplit` and `SharesSplit` — distribute remainder cents deterministically.
- **BigDecimal / cents only** — never floating point.
- **Per-group lock** for balance mutations; reads can use a snapshot.
- **Edits / deletes via reverse expenses** to maintain history.
- **Multi-currency:** store original; convert at view time.
- **Composition + interfaces;** no `EqualExpense extends Expense` hierarchy.

sections.title: How to Answer This Verbally
sections.content:
**Problem framing**

Splitwise tracks who paid for what among a group and who owes whom. Design pressure: multiple split modes (equal, exact, percent, shares); maintaining balance sheet incrementally (don't recompute from scratch); settling up (minimize number of transfers when 4 people have tangled debts); edge cases (rounding, multi-currency, payer in participants).

LLD-level: single-instance OO design unless asked about scale. Strategy choices and simplification algorithm are the grade.

**Clarifying questions**

Groups required or two-friend splits outside groups. Split modes (equal, exact per person, percentage, shares like A:2/B:1). Currency single or multi. Settlement (record cash repayments? compute simplification?). Edit/delete expenses (adds reconciliation). Persistence. Concurrency (multiple users adding expenses simultaneously).

**Assumptions**

Expenses live in a Group; two-friend splits modeled as special group. Four split modes: EQUAL, EXACT, PERCENT, SHARES. Single currency core; multi-currency as extension. Settling records cash repayments + supports simplification on demand. Edits/deletes as extension (reversal of original split). In-memory with GroupRepository interface. Concurrent expense additions in same group; per-group lock on balance updates.

**Core entities**

User: immutable id + name + email.
Group: list of members, list of expenses, BalanceSheet.
Expense: immutable record (id, payer, total, currency, description, splits per participant, timestamp).
Split: (user, amount). Sum == expense total.
SplitStrategy interface: computeSplits(total, participants, params) → List<Split>. One impl per mode.
BalanceSheet: Map<UserId, Map<UserId, Money>> 'A owes B'. Incremental updates on expense add. netBalance(a, b).
SettlementStrategy interface: simplify(BalanceSheet) → List<Transfer>. Default = greedy creditor/debtor matching.
Transfer: (from, to, amount).
SplitwiseService: facade — addExpense, recordSettlement, getBalances, getSimplifiedTransfers.

**Split strategies**

All implement same interface; differ in how to break total into per-user Splits.

EqualSplit: convert to cents, integer-divide, distribute remainder cents to first N participants for fairness. perHead = totalCents / n; remainder = totalCents - perHead*n; for i in 0..n: cents = perHead + (i < remainder ? 1 : 0).

PercentSplit: requires SplitParams.percents map. Validate sum == 100. Each participant's share = total * percent / 100.

SharesSplit: requires SplitParams.shares map (weights). totalShares = sum. Each share = total * weight / totalShares; same remainder distribution as EqualSplit.

Rounding rule for EQUAL and SHARES: convert to integer cents, integer-divide, distribute remaining cents one each to first N participants. Documented and predictable; no floating point. Same rule for refunds on delete.

**Balance sheet — incremental updates**

Recomputing from all expenses every time is wasteful. Maintain incrementally.

Matrix: outer key debtor, inner key creditor, value amount owed. matrix[debtor][creditor] = cents owed.

applyExpense(e): for each Split, skip payer's own share. Else s.user() owes e.paidBy() s.amount() — adjust(debtor=s.user(), creditor=e.paidBy(), amount).

applyTransfer(t): t.from pays t.to — reduces from's debt to to. adjust(debtor=t.to, creditor=t.from, amount).

adjust: compute net = currentBalance + amount. Normalize — keep only one direction per pair non-zero. If positive, store debtor → creditor; remove reverse. If negative, flip and store creditor → debtor. If zero, remove both.

Normalization keeps matrix small and lookups O(1). Avoids 'A owes B 10, B owes A 7' redundancy.

**Settle up — greedy simplification**

Tangled debt graph; find minimum number of transfers. Exact minimum is NP-hard; standard approximation is greedy max-creditor / max-debtor pairing — near-optimal in practice.

Algorithm:
1. Compute each user's net balance (credits - debts)
2. Max-heap of creditors (positive balances), max-heap of debtors (most negative balances)
3. While both non-empty: take largest creditor C and largest debtor D. Transfer = min(|C|, |D|). Emit Transfer(D → C, transfer). Adjust balances; remove if zero.

For 4-5 people: typically 2-3 transfers instead of 6+ pairwise. O(N log N) where N = users with non-zero balance.

**End-to-end flow — add expense + settle**

Alice paid $30 dinner for [Alice, Bob, Carol] EQUAL split.

Svc.addExpense → EqualSplit.computeSplits($30, [Alice, Bob, Carol]) → [Alice $10, Bob $10, Carol $10] → Group.addExpense → BalanceSheet.applyExpense → Bob → Alice +$10, Carol → Alice +$10.

Later: getSimplifiedTransfers → [Bob → Alice $10, Carol → Alice $10].

Bob actually pays → Svc.recordSettlement(Transfer(Bob → Alice $10)) → BalanceSheet.applyTransfer → Bob's debt cleared.

**Concurrency**

Two boundaries:

1. Per-group balance updates: applyExpense and applyTransfer mutate the matrix. Acquire per-group ReentrantLock for the duration. Cross-group operations don't contend.

2. Reads: getBalances and getSimplifiedTransfers should be consistent snapshots. Either copy under same lock, or ReadWriteLock (writers exclusive, readers shared).

Real distributed: per-group state in DB with optimistic lock on group's version field; all becomes a single transaction. Interview-level fine with in-memory locks.

**Failure modes and edge cases**

- Rounding remainder: $10 / 3 → [$3.34, $3.33, $3.33]. Document rule (extra cent to first N, deterministic)
- Payer in participants: own split doesn't generate self-debt; skip in applyExpense
- Edit/delete expense: apply reverse expense, then new one. Audit log; never lose history
- Multi-currency: store original-currency amounts in expense; balance sheet per original currency. Conversion is view concern, not storage. Settlement handles multi-currency or normalizes first
- Floating point: never. BigDecimal (cents) or custom Money value object
- Cycle of debts: simplification handles naturally — nets to zero → no transfer
- Self-transfer: Transfer(A → A) invalid; reject at construction
- User leaving group with non-zero balance: require settlement first; record final transfer log

**Extensibility**

- New split mode (ITEMIZED restaurant bill where each line maps to specific eaters): new SplitStrategy impl. No other changes
- New settlement strategy (minimize transfers constrained to existing creditor/debtor edges): new SettlementStrategy
- Multi-currency: CurrencyConverter port; balance sheet per currency or convert at view time
- Reminders/notifications: publish BalanceUpdatedEvent when balance large or stale
- Receipt OCR / auto-import: ExpenseSource adapter parses receipts → Expense objects
- Analytics: expense history becomes CQRS read model; main aggregate stays clean

**Trade-offs and alternatives**

- Incremental matrix vs recompute on read: incremental O(1) reads but careful update logic. Recompute simple but O(N²) per query. Active groups → incremental wins
- Greedy simplification vs optimal (NP): greedy near-optimal in practice; optimal exponential, not worth it
- In-memory vs persistent: in-memory fine for interview; production wraps Group as JPA aggregate with BalanceSheetEmbeddable and @Version
- Strategy interface vs enum+switch: Strategy scales as modes grow; lets each mode's params live with impl. Enum+switch fits 2 modes, then bloats
- Per-group lock vs lock-free: lock correct + simple; lock-free overkill for low-contention domain
- Single vs multi-currency: single right starting point. Multi-currency adds conversion semantics that should be deliberate design, not afterthought

**Recommendation**

**Build Splitwise around three entities (User, Group, Expense) with a SplitStrategy interface for the split modes (Equal, Exact, Percent, Shares) and a SettlementStrategy interface for simplification. Maintain the BalanceSheet incrementally as a normalized debtor→creditor matrix; never recompute from scratch. Use the greedy max-creditor / max-debtor algorithm to minimize transfers (near-optimal in practice; exact is NP-hard). Always work in cents / BigDecimal; document the remainder distribution rule. Per-group ReentrantLock around mutations is enough for the interview level; production maps cleanly to a JPA aggregate with optimistic locking. Multi-currency, edit/delete, and notifications are clear extensions that drop in without touching the core flow.**

followup_questions: Walk through the greedy simplification algorithm with 4 users and a tangled debt graph.
How do you handle rounding so $10 split among 3 doesn't introduce a phantom cent?
What changes for multi-currency support, and where would you place the conversion?
How would you implement edit/delete of an expense without losing history?

seo.metaDescription: Low-Level Design for an expense-sharing app: User/Group/Expense entities, SplitStrategy (Equal/Exact/Percent/Shares) and SettlementStrategy (greedy simplification), incremental balance sheet, rounding and multi-currency handling.
